frame: DRAW_LINE(emitter: marker pixel | port cell | every cell of an object's leading face or span; direction: one of 8, from shape/port/position or learned; colour: emitter or learned, solid or every k-th cell; stop: grid edge | first obstacle | target line/wall; on-hit: none | recolour | erase | stamp)
definition: For each emitter cell (an isolated marker, an odd-coloured port cell, or each cell/row/column of an object's face), step repeatedly along a direction d and paint background cells in the emitter colour (optionally dotted). Stop at the grid edge, the first non-background cell or a designated wall/line, and optionally apply a hit effect such as recolouring the obstacle, erasing what the ray touches, or calling a stamp at the meeting point.
verbnet_like: line-drawing: shoot / cast / extend / draw ray, beam, trail, laser
why_general: Rays, beams, shadows and extrusions from seeds to the border or an obstacle are among the most frequent ARC motifs in both ARC-1 and ARC-2, and differ only in emitter, direction and stop parameters.

frame: WALK(agent: seed pixel | vehicle | beam head; initial heading from shape, nose or legend; turn rule: bounce off surface | turn when blocked | hug obstacle edge | next legend command | scheduled arm lengths (spiral); paint trail: yes/no; stop: exits grid | reaches goal | boxed in)
definition: Simulate an agent that starts at a seed with a heading and moves one cell per step, painting its trail (or only its final position). At each step a pluggable turn rule decides the new heading (reflect off a mirror, turn or sidestep when blocked, follow an obstacle edge, execute the next legend instruction, or turn after an arm of scheduled length), and the walk stops when the agent leaves the grid, reaches a goal object or cannot move.
verbnet_like: motion with path: walk / climb / drive / bounce / spiral / navigate
VerbNet run-51.3.2, roll-51.3.1 with path PP
why_general: Path tracing with turns (spirals, bouncing lasers, obstacle-hugging climbers, legend-programmed turtles, planners) recurs heavily in ARC-2 and is one step simulator with a swappable turn rule.

frame: MOVE(object | pixel | split half; direction: toward wall/gravity side | along attached tail/track/arm | colour-to-direction table | learned; distance: constant | tail length (tail erased) | until contact with wall, edge or settled object | to grid edge; mode: move | copy)
definition: Select the movable objects (loose shapes, single pixels, rectangles with tails, halves of a split shape) and translate each rigidly along a direction derived from a wall, the gravity side, its attached tail, a colour table or training. The distance is a learned constant, the length of the attached tail/track (which is then erased), or 'until contact' with a wall, the grid edge or an already-settled object, processing objects nearest-first so they stack.
verbnet_like: motion: slide / shift / move / fall / drop / drift / push / dock
why_general: Rigid translation with a derived direction and a stop-at-contact or tail-length distance (gravity, docking, sliding along a track) is a core ARC physics prior.

frame: REFLECT(shape | half-pattern; symmetry element: axis line object | marker cell or segment as point/plane mirror | centre line of a bracket frame | grid midlines / quadrants | 90-degree rotation centre; write image on the other side; recolour image: keep | swap | marker colour; erase strays)
definition: Find the symmetry element (a full-length axis line, a marker cell/segment acting as point or plane mirror, the centre line of a frame, or the grid's midlines) and write the reflected or rotated image of the shape on the opposite side so the figure becomes symmetric. Optionally recolour the image or the original (swap colours, marker colour) and erase cells outside the completed figure.
verbnet_like: reflection: mirror / reflect / flip / unfold / rotate-copy
VerbNet: no direct class; WordNet reflect.v.03, flip.v.02
why_general: Symmetry completion about an explicit or implicit axis is one of the canonical ARC priors and only the choice of symmetry element varies.

frame: SURROUND(source: seed pixel | object | room walls | canvas border; metric: Chebyshev (or Manhattan); colour by distance d: palette[d] for d < k (halo/frame of thickness k, k from a count, a size or training) | palette[d mod P] (concentric rings, ripples, revolution profile); paint background only)
definition: Compute for every cell its Chebyshev distance d to a source set (a seed pixel, an object, a room's walls or the canvas border). Paint background cells with palette[d] while d < k to get a halo or frame of thickness k (k read from a count, a block size or training), or with palette[d mod P] to get periodic concentric rings, ripples or a revolved profile.
verbnet_like: surrounding: frame / ring / halo / outline / inflate / ripple
why_general: Halos, frames and concentric rings are all distance-field colourings, so one distance transform with a thresholded or periodic palette covers outlines, ripples and onion-skin patterns in unseen tasks.

frame: STAMP(stencil: learned from training | template found in grid | legend sign | same-colour die; anchor: each marker pixel | line crossing | midpoint of a marker pair | ray meeting point | plate centre; alignment: centred | corner; colours: learned per stencil role; paint background only)
definition: Locate anchor points (isolated marker pixels, line crossings, midpoints of marker pairs, points where a ray meets a line) and paste a small stencil on each anchor, such as the diagonal neighbours, a plus, a 3x3 ring or a house glyph. The stencil and its role colours are induced from training or read from a template or legend in the grid, and it is painted over background unless the task overwrites.
verbnet_like: copying: stamp / paste / replicate / decorate / punch
why_general: Replacing each marker or crossing by a fixed local decoration is a generic 'local rewrite at keypoints' operation that recurs whenever a task decorates points.

frame: TILE(motif: whole input | cropped window | per-colour block | downscaled unit tile; layout mask: all-ones k x k | the input's own coloured cells (fractal) | mask from another panel | selected row/diagonal | first N slots where N is a tally; also inverse: compress block-scaled pattern to its unit)
definition: Build the output as mask (x) motif: place a copy of the motif (the input, a cropped window, a per-colour learned block, or a unit tile recovered by downscaling) at every cell of a layout mask (all ones, the input's own coloured cells, a mask taken from another panel, a selected row or diagonal, or the first N slots where N is a count). Optionally run a cell-level post-rule on the tiled result, and support the inverse direction (detect block scale, reduce, re-tile).
verbnet_like: repetition: tile / repeat / upscale / enlarge / blow up / Kronecker product
VerbNet multiply (not native), WordNet tile.v.01, scale.v.03
why_general: Grid-level tiling and scaling (self-tiling, mask-driven tiling, per-cell block substitution) is one of the oldest ARC priors and the mask/motif parametrisation covers its many variants.

frame: CONNECT(two items sharing a colour/marker: pixels | lattice cells | tiles | edge markers | facing parallel segments or rectangles; alignment: same row, column or diagonal with clear line of sight; paint between (strict or inclusive): their colour | new colour | learned map of crossed colours; overlaps: learned combine)
definition: Find pairs of items (pixels, lattice cells, framed tiles, edge markers, or facing segments/rectangles) that share a colour or marker and are aligned on a common row, column or diagonal. Paint the cells between them with their colour, a new colour or a learned map of the crossed colours, combining overlaps by a learned rule.
verbnet_like: connection: connect / join / bridge / link / span
why_general: Joining aligned like-coloured items with a straight bridge is a basic grouping-by-similarity prior that appears at pixel, tile and object scale.

frame: COPY(template: the one patterned panel/box in a separator lattice or framed-box lattice; targets: all | empty | same frame colour | even lattice offset | marker-indexed panel | blank Raven cell; per-target transform: identity | rotation/reflection by position | recolour by row key | stretch to margins)
definition: Split the grid into panels with full separator lines or framed boxes and identify the template panel (the only patterned one, or the one holding a marker). Copy its pattern into the target panels selected by a rule (all, empty, same frame colour, even offset, the one indexed by the marker's in-panel position), applying a per-target transform such as a positional rotation/reflection or recolouring by that row's key.
why_general: Separator lattices with one exemplar panel are a staple ARC layout, and copying the exemplar into rule-selected panels is the usual intended operation.

frame: COUNT(category: colour | object shape | connected component | rung | counter; tally = cell or object count (optionally difference); render: bar / square / bead run of length = count; order: by count | fixed colour order; place: chart panel | new grid)
definition: Tally a category (cells per colour, objects per shape or colour, rungs per ladder, counters per abacus) and render each tally as a bar, solid square or run of marker cells whose length or area equals the count. Order the bars by count or by a fixed colour order and lay them out in a blank chart panel or a new grid whose size follows the largest count.
verbnet_like: VerbNet calculate-? (no class), WordNet count.v.01, tally.v.02
why_general: Turning a count into a length (histograms, tallies, bar charts) is a standard numerosity prior that reappears whenever the output size depends on how many of something there are.

frame: FIT(loose piece; target: socket / notch / hole / pin stack in a fixed body, or matching marker/connector cells on another piece or board; search: translations x 8 rigid transforms; criterion: exact complement without overlap | marker coincidence | connector adjacency | equal label; result: move piece | recolour fitting pieces | crop assembly)
definition: For each loose piece, search translations (and rotations/reflections when allowed) for the placement where its cells exactly fill a hole or notch of a fixed body without overlap, or where its marker/connector cells coincide with or abut matching cells of the target. Move the piece there (or recolour it if it fits), erase the original, and crop to the assembly when the output is just the assembled shape.
verbnet_like: fitting: fit / insert / plug / dock / assemble / key into lock
why_general: Shape-complement and connector matching (jigsaw, key/lock, mortise/tenon) is a frequent ARC-2 theme and reduces to one placement search with a pluggable fit criterion.

frame: COVER(target: a blob to tile | scattered marker evidence | partial V or plus; pieces: plus / cross / square / bar / L / 3x3 window / structuring element, shapes and sizes from training; constraint: non-overlapping, explain all evidence, fewest pieces; paint: missing cells with fill colour | each piece by its type colour | union of fitting translates (opening))
definition: Enumerate placements of small template pieces (shapes and sizes induced from training) that fit the target, i.e. tile a blob exactly or explain scattered marker cells with the fewest non-overlapping pieces. Paint the chosen placements: fill their missing cells with the fill colour, or recolour each piece by its shape type.
why_general: Recognising known parts under partial evidence (hidden pluses, piece decompositions, morphological opening) is a general perceptual-completion prior.

frame: LOCATE-RECT(delimiters: bounding box of a marker group (inset/outset d) | four corner brackets / crop marks | two parallel lines | broken lattice crossings | start/end marker pair | hollow frame; op: draw outline | fill or recolour inside | crop (concatenate several) | crop and fit the loose shape inside by integer scaling, moving or mirroring)
definition: Detect rectangles implied by delimiters: the bounding box of a group of marker cells (optionally inset or snapped to separators), the span of corner brackets or of two parallel lines, the cells between start/end markers, or a hollow frame. Then apply one operation: draw its outline, fill or recolour its inside, crop it out (stacking several crops), or crop it and fit the loose shape into its interior by integer scaling, translation or mirroring.
verbnet_like: extraction: crop / cut out / extract / frame
why_general: Inferring a rectangle from sparse delimiters (corners, marks, a frame) and then drawing, filling or cropping it is a recurring Gestalt-closure prior in both datasets.

frame: ARRANGE(objects | crops | strips; sort key: reading order | colour | size | count | genus | occlusion layer | self-indicated slot; layout: row | column stacks | diagonal chain | 2x2 or 3x3 slot grid; gap g; crop output)
definition: Extract the objects (or cropped strips), compute a sort key (reading order, colour, size, topological genus, occlusion layer, or the slot their own marks indicate), and lay them out contiguously along an axis, in per-key column stacks, as a diagonal chain, or into a small slot grid with gap g. Output the packed canvas cropped to its content (or of a learned size).
verbnet_like: sorting / arrangement: sort / stack / gather / line up / restack / concatenate
why_general: Gathering objects and re-laying them in a sorted contiguous layout is a general rearrangement prior whose only parameters are the key and the layout.

frame: FILL(each row and/or column within scope: grid | frame interior | object bbox; predicate: entirely background | contains a coloured cell | mostly filled (broken line) | between two bars/markers | below or above a wall | extremal profile column; fill: background cells with new colour | nearest coloured cell along the line)
definition: Iterate over the rows and/or columns inside a scope (the grid, a frame interior or an object's bounding box) and evaluate a line predicate: entirely background, contains a coloured cell, mostly filled, lies between two bars, lies below/above a wall, or is the extremal column of a profile. Fill the background cells of every qualifying line with the target colour (or propagate the nearest coloured cell along the line).
verbnet_like: filling: fill / flood / paint across / complete broken line
why_general: Row/column-wise fills gated by a simple line predicate are cheap, frequent ARC rules that a predicate library plus a scope selector covers.

frame: SUBSTITUTE(field objects or blocks; table key->value read from an in-grid legend: fenced corner box | key row/column | colour pairs | header list | indicator column | panels of a strip; value: colour | glyph/shape | ring order | turn instruction | print parameter)
definition: Find the legend region (a fenced corner box, a key row/column on the border, adjacent colour pairs, or a strip of labelled panels) and parse it into a key->value table, where keys are colours, shapes or positions and values are colours, glyphs or instructions. Apply the table to every object or block in the main field, substituting its colour or replacing it by the mapped glyph, and remove the legend if the outputs do.
verbnet_like: mapping via key: look up / translate / decode / render legend
why_general: In-grid legends that bind colours to colours, glyphs or instructions are a hallmark of ARC-2 and only the legend parser and the value type vary.

frame: RECOLOUR(target: object | enclosed region | room | cell | row | quadrant; colour source: the seed contained in it | the marker touching it | the nearest marker or line (Voronoi) | plurality of touching markers; ties: keep | crossing colour)
definition: For each target (an object, an enclosed region or room, a quadrant, a row or a single cell), find the seed/marker that lies inside it, touches it, or is nearest to it by Manhattan/Chebyshev distance (plurality vote if several). Recolour the target (or its background/interior cells) with that seed's colour, leaving ties unchanged or giving them a designated colour.
verbnet_like: change-of-colour by proximity: take colour of / inherit / flood with seed colour
why_general: Inheriting colour from the contained or nearest marker is a general binding rule that reappears whenever a task places colour hints next to uncoloured shapes.

frame: EXTRAPOLATE(unit term: stripe/line pair | row block | motif | panel | run | concentric ring; step T: shift by period | shift with growing gap | grow by one | scale by c | rotate slots | colour cycle; until: grid edge | one more term; repair mode: overwrite cells disagreeing with the period)
definition: Identify the unit term(s) of a progression in the grid (a stripe pair, row block, motif, panel or run) and infer the step transform between terms: a translation by a period, a growing gap, growth by one cell, scaling by a factor, a cyclic slot rotation or a colour cycle. Apply the step repeatedly until the grid edge (or once to produce the next panel), and in repair mode overwrite cells that disagree with the inferred periodic pattern.
verbnet_like: repetition / extrapolation: repeat / continue / propagate / next term / periodic
VerbNet repeat (no class), WordNet extrapolate.v.02, repeat.v.01
why_general: Inferring a period or term-to-term step from a partial sequence and continuing it is a classic inductive prior (Raven/number-series style) that recurs across ARC.

frame: SELECT(candidates: panels | tiles | regions | objects | columns | diagonal runs | candidate shapes; score: uniqueness among near-copies (odd one out) | min/max cell count | largest growth between parts | longest run | best template match; output: crop the winner | 1x1 of its colour | mark it in place | enlarge it)
definition: Enumerate comparable candidates (panels, tiles, regions, objects, columns, runs, or candidate shapes) and compute a score: dissimilarity to the others (odd one out), a cell count, a growth, a run length, or a template-match quality. Output the winning candidate cropped, as a 1x1 cell of its colour, marked in place, or enlarged.
verbnet_like: selection: select / pick / choose / find odd one out / rank
why_general: Choosing the unique or extremal item among comparable candidates is a very common ARC output rule and decomposes into a candidate generator, a score and a selector.

frame: LOOKUP(key: whole-grid feature (binary shape mask, number of colours, dominant colour, panel hole pattern, connectivity predicate) | structural role of a cell or region (corner/edge/centre cell of a partition, convex/concave outline corner, quadrant or inset of a rectangle, centre of an odd square); value: output glyph | colour; table induced from training pairs)
definition: Compute a discrete key, either a global feature of the input (shape mask, colour count, most frequent colour, a panel's hole pattern, a yes/no predicate) or the structural role of each cell/region (its position class in a partition, convex vs concave corner, quadrant or inner inset). Look the key up in a table induced from the training pairs and emit the stored glyph for global keys, or paint each cell/region with the stored colour for role keys.
verbnet_like: classification + mapping: select by / determined by / looked up from training
why_general: Many tasks only require mapping a discrete feature or positional role to an output memorised from the training pairs, so a feature library plus an induced table transfers to unseen tasks of this kind.
